'''Richard Steven Ellis''' (May 15, 1947 – July 2, 2018) was an American mathematician.

He was born on May 15, 1947, in [[Brookline, Massachusetts]], to parents Murray and Helen. Ellis graduated from [[Boston Latin School]] and attended [[Harvard University]], where he studied German literature and mathematics. He pursued graduate study at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]]. In 1972, he received his PhD from the [[New York University]] for his thesis ''Chapman-Eskog-Hilbert Expansion for Models of the Boltzmann Equation'' under the supervision of [[Henry McKean]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Mathematics genealogy project |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=33264}}</ref> He began teaching at [[Northwestern University]] and left for the [[University of Massachusetts Amherst]] in 1975.<ref>{{cite news |title=Obituary: Richard Ellis, Professor of Mathematics and Statistics |url=http://www.umass.edu/newsoffice/article/obituary-richard-ellis-professor |accessdate=July 17, 2018 |publisher=University of Massachusetts Amherst |date=July 5, 2018}}</ref> In 1984, he improved a key result in [[large deviations theory]] originally due to [[Jürgen Gärtner]], which is now known as Gärtner-Ellis Theorem. He was named fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] in 1999.<ref>{{cite news |title=Honored IMS Fellows |url=https://www.imstat.org/honored-ims-fellows/ |accessdate=July 17, 2018 |publisher=Institute of Mathematical Statistics}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Curriculum vitae |url=http://people.math.umass.edu/~rsellis/Shorter-CV-new.pdf |accessdate=July 17, 2018}}</ref> Ellis died of bile duct cancer in New York City on July 2, 2018, aged 71.<ref>{{cite news |title=Richard S. Ellis (1947–2018) |url=http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/gazettenet/obituary.aspx?page=lifestory&pid=189466520 |accessdate=July 17, 2018 |work=Daily Hampshire Gazette |date=July 5, 2018}}</ref>
